Analysis workflow and interpretation

Source: vignettes/articles/analysis-workflow.Rmd
analysis-workflow.Rmd

MERIDIAN connects seven modules. The main analytical workflow is interactive; the examples here use exported helpers and the bundled simulated data.

1. Map data and experimental design

In Overview, map the identifiers and numeric traits. Specify RCBD, incomplete-block or augmented design as appropriate. Blocks are nested within replicate and environment. Select replicated check genotypes for augmented designs. A design label alone cannot resolve missing replication or confounded effects; inspect the validation messages.

2. Inspect measurements

Use Traits for distributions, G×E means, missingness, environment correlations and outliers. Check whether absent measurements affect a few plots or entire genotype–environment cells. Each trait may have different coverage.

3. Fit ANOVA and mixed models

In ANOVA, choose a trait and selection objective, then run the analysis.

  • The fixed analysis uses adjusted marginal tests for genotype and environment and a partial G×E test. Partial sums of squares are not additive variance percentages.
  • Variance components use REML. Cullis generalized heritability is derived from pairwise prediction-error variances.
  • BLUEs treat genotype as fixed and include design and G×E terms.
  • BLUPs treat genotype and G×E as random, with environment fixed. Predictions average environments equally. Prediction intervals include fixed-effect estimation uncertainty, conditional on the estimated variance components.

Review singularity, replication and estimability diagnostics alongside the estimates. A ranking does not by itself establish a significant difference.

4. Study stability

Stability includes AMMI, GGE, Eberhart–Russell, Wricke and Shukla outputs. Read the processing tables before comparing results. AMMI/GGE can complete missing cell means using an estimable additive model in a connected network; these predictions remain distinct from observed means. Classical stability indices use a disclosed complete-cell subset.

AMMI ANOVA uses observed plot data and the design; it does not treat imputed means as extra observations. Without plot-error degrees of freedom, interpret the decomposition descriptively.

5. Explore adaptation and environmental covariates

Adaptation combines observed-winner grouping, reaction norms, environmental PCA, correlations and climatic-driver plots. Winner groups display ties and coverage; they are exploratory groupings rather than validated mega-environments.

You can supply precomputed numeric covariates. Environmental data with latitude, longitude and planting/harvest dates can request daily NASA POWER weather. If harvest dates are missing, the workflow may estimate a crop-cycle duration and reports a warning; check those dates against the actual trial.

Example: calculate weather summaries offline

The following small series is simulated to demonstrate the helper. It is not a weather record or a fitted crop model.

daily <- data.frame(
  T2M_MAX = c(25, 27, 24, 28, 31, 29),
  T2M_MIN = c(15, 17, 14, 18, 21, 19),
  PRECTOTCORR = c(2, 5, 0, 10, 1, 0),
  RH2M = c(60, 70, 50, 65, 80, 75),
  ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN = c(18, 20, 15, 22, 19, 21)
)
MERIDIAN::calculate_enviromic_indices(daily, dtf_mean = 2, dtm_mean = 4)
#>   MeanTemp_C TotalRainfall_mm GDD MeanRH_pct TotalSolar_MJ GDD_Veg
#> 1      22.33               18  74      66.67           115      22
#>   TotalRainfall_Veg MeanTemp_Veg GDD_Rep TotalRainfall_Rep MeanTemp_Rep
#> 1                 7           21      22                10           21
#>   HeatStressDays_Rep GDD_Late TotalRainfall_Late MeanTemp_Late
#> 1                  0       30                  1            25

This helper currently calculates growing degree days with a base temperature of 10 °C and reproductive heat-stress days above 30 °C. These fixed thresholds are not automatically calibrated to the chosen crop. Stage boundaries use supplied mean days to flowering and maturity; check that they match your biological question.

Dates can also be standardized before preparing environmental data:

MERIDIAN::parse_date_robustly(c("2026-05-21", "21/05/2026", "46163"))
#> [1] "2026-05-21" "2026-05-21" "2026-05-21"

Use ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD) to avoid ambiguity between day/month and month/day formats.

6. Inspect spatial patterns

In Field Map, select an environment and trait and specify field row/column coordinates. Fit a SpATS model and inspect its diagnostics, spatial trend, variance components and adjusted genotype means. Fixed genotype effects cannot be separated from spatial trends when layout positions perfectly confound them; this applies to the bundled example and is diagnosed by the app.

The across-environment spatial summary averages separate fits descriptively. Its standard error assumes independence. It is not a joint spatial MET model or a fitted second-stage MET analysis.

7. Register and export results

Use the explicit Send … to Reports controls to retain outputs. Registered plots and tables are snapshots with metadata and dataset identity. The Reports module lets you inspect them, change export styling, build composed figures and generate HTML/PDF reports. Downloads apply current export settings even if a preview has not been refreshed.

Interpretation and limits

  • Identifiers must be complete and experimental units unique. Missing trait values are handled per analysis; non-finite observed measurements are invalid.
  • Mixed models assume independent G×E effects and homogeneous plot-error variance. Factor-analytic covariance structures are not implemented.
  • Environmental associations are exploratory. Correlation with weather does not establish a causal driver or validate a selection rule.
  • Stage-specific weather indices use fixed temperature thresholds, and any estimated harvest dates require validation against trial records.
  • Observe the reported imputation, coverage and exclusions when interpreting stability and adaptation results.
  • Spatial means across environments are descriptive summaries of separate fits.

For a reproducible report, retain the original input, column mapping, design, selection direction, model settings and registered outputs.
